card.title: Belonging on Changing Terms
card.instruction: Seek acceptance by adapting quickly, then let each adaptation create a new version of yourself you must defend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bought this jacket for my first supper at your sailing club. Will I fit in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're casual. Roll your sleeves up; I'll introduce you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There. I'm one of those relaxed old hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Lovely. I'll tell them you're new so they'll explain things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say I'm returning. You can explain the boats privately. These sleeves suggest I already know.

mechanism: A adapts dress to gain club acceptance and then defends the experienced identity the adaptation implies.
confusable: Unlike pretending expertise from the start, B's acceptance advice must create a new persona A tries to maintain.
comparison: S233-a hides newcomer lessons behind rolled sleeves; S233-b asks a sister to hear a new listener identity instead of a failed climber.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
